::: {#exr-miller-taylor-product-cos-log}
#### Taylor series of a product of known expansions

Adapted from @problifesavercalc, Question 1.1.29.

Find the terms up to degree 2 of the Taylor series for

$$f(x) = \cos(x)\log(1 + x)$$

at $x_0 = 0$.
:::

::: {#sol-miller-taylor-product-cos-log}
Multiply the known Maclaurin expansions:

$$\ba
\cos x &= 1 - \frac{x^2}{2} + O(x^4)
\\
\log(1 + x) &= x - \frac{x^2}{2} + O(x^3)
\ea$$

Multiplying and dropping terms of order $x^3$ and higher:

$$f(x) = \paren{1 - \frac{x^2}{2} + \dots}\paren{x - \frac{x^2}{2} + \dots} = x - \frac{x^2}{2} + O(x^3)$$
:::
